To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intracerebroven-tricular infusion of tetro-dotoxin for 2-7 days reduced the number of ouabain binding sites and the maximal transport capacity of brain Na+, K(+)-ATP-ase, measured as 86Rb + uptake, in a dose-dependent manner.

intracerebroven-tricular infusion of 1-3 micrograms/h of tetrod- toxin for 4 days decreased the number of Na+K+ATPase sites and reduced the maximal transport capacity of Na+K+-ATP-ase in cerebral cortex.
the intracerebrovetricular administration of the sodium channel blocker, tetrodotoxine, reduces the number and function of brain sodium-potassium pumps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Na+,K+-activated ATPase activity in the central nervous system.
the role of Na+,K+-pump in the regulation of the neuronal function and with its possible role in the pathophysiology of neurological disorders.
the regulation of Na+,K+- ATPase activity and function in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intracerebroven-tricular infusion of tetrodo-toxin reduces the activity and function of Na+,K+- ATPase, and that this reduction in activity is not specific for high or low affinity ouabain-binding sites.
the effect of intracerebventricular infusion of 1 or more microgram/h of tetrodotorin is to decrease the activity of Na+,K+-dependent transport in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intracerebroventricular tetrodotox in reduced brain Na+,K+- ATPase activity by reducing the number of Na+K+ ATPase sites and reducing the functional capacity of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+,K(+),ATPase in the brain is highly sensitive to tetrodotoxins, which are commonly used to study the effects of neuronal depolarization on ion transport in the brain.
the Na,K-ATPase can be regulated by the activity of NaV channels.
the Na+,K+- ATPase is an important target for the effects of tetrodtoxin.
